name: Ironpass Thermal Work Layer
description:
A heavyweight crew-neck thermal built for people who work outdoors in the Great Lakes corridor from October through April. The Ironpass is not stylish — it is effective. Double-knit construction with a waffle interior and a smooth exterior face, available in charcoal, navy, and a faded brick red. The collar is high enough to protect the neck from wind without being a turtleneck. Seams are flatlock-stitched to prevent bunching under gear. Thumb loops at the cuffs.

Construction crews, port workers, and utility teams all wear these. The fabric is dense and slightly stiff when new, softening over months of use into something almost comfortable. It smells faintly of the factory when new — a smell longtime wearers associate with the start of a cold season and a paycheck.
what_it_says: You work outside. You don't have time for anything that doesn't function. You've probably owned three of these.
story_hooks: A particular batch of Ironpass thermals was sold to a construction crew that vanished during a tunnel excavation project — some of the shirts have since shown up at the Gray Zone market stalls.
Ironpass recently lost a contract with a major corponation and is quietly going under; workers who've worn nothing else for twenty years are facing a brand extinction.
A union organizer uses an Ironpass thermal as a kind of unofficial identifier — if you're wearing one at a certain meeting, you know what the meeting is really about.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian crew-neck thermal with substantial presence—neither fitted nor loose, but deliberately engineered for function over form. The high crew collar sits protective at the base of the neck. Sleeves are straight and purposeful, ending in cuff thumb loops that suggest hands perpetually gloved. The silhouette reads as 'working class' at a glance—substantial weight, no decoration, built to layer.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with enough room for layering underneath; sleeves sit close to the wrist without tapering. Cut long enough to stay tucked through physical labor. Not slim, not oversized—calibrated for freedom of movement under heavier outerwear.
physical_description.primary_material: Double-knit synthetic thermal blend—dense, durable, designed for temperature regulation in sub-zero conditions. Factory-sourced from GLMZ textile mills.
physical_description.texture: Exterior face is smooth and slightly mechanically finished; interior reveals a pronounced waffle knit that traps air for insulation. Fabric is stiff and slightly plastic-feeling when new, breaking in to a softer hand after weeks of wear. Seams are flatlock-stitched and sit flush against skin—no interior chafe points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal (most common), navy, or faded brick red—all muted, practical tones that hide wear and dirt. No patterns, no branding visible from a distance.
physical_description.closures: Pull-over crew neck; no zippers, buttons, or magnetic snaps. Thumb loops at each cuff are friction-fit elastic.
distinctive_features: High protective crew collar without turtleneck bulk
Flatlock seams throughout for comfort under hard gear
Thumb loop cuffs that anchor the layer while wearing work gloves
Double-knit waffle interior visible at cuffs and collar
Deliberate stiffness in new garments that softens with use
Factory chemical smell that fades after first wash
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class functional)—this is the uniform of people paid hourly for labor, not status dressing.
physical_description.cultural_context: Construction crews, port workers, utilities, outdoor logistics—anyone who works in the GLMZ winter corridor. Wearing one signals: 'I work outside. I work hard. I buy what works, not what impresses.' Authentic working-class identity, zero corporate flourish.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in over months; the stiffness gradually softens to comfort. Visible wear patterns emerge at cuffs and collar from repeated friction against gear and skin. May show faint water stains, minor snags, slight discoloration from sweat and weather. Older units show significant fading, especially in brick red colorway.
